problem_statement: Return a new list containing each integer from values exactly once, in first-occurrence order. values is any Python list of integers (excluding bool), including an empty list. Do not modify the input.
valid_input_domain: Return a new list containing each integer from values exactly once, in first-occurrence order. values is any Python list of integers (excluding bool), including an empty list. Do not modify the input.
bug_explanation: Sorting removes duplicates but changes the required first-occurrence order.
provenance: Custom pilot example, drafted with AI assistance. Not copied from a benchmark; no novelty claim.

human_review_record.notes: Specification, reference solution, faulty solution and named counterexample verified. Bug confirmed: sorted(set(...)) removes duplicates but a set does not guarantee first-occurrence order; the explicit sorted() then imposes numeric order. Counterexample order_matters [3,1,3,2] discussed. Note: ascending is a false pass because first-occurrence order coincidentally matches numeric order for that input.
